rule: Every storage write fixture must show a backend write smoke expectation before route tests or backend implementation begin.
phase_one_guardrail: No rental payment, deposit, escrow, payout, booking commission, payment-custody signal, tenant-private memory, or un-smoked write fixture can reach backend implementation in phase one.
smoke_principles: Turn each storage write fixture into a visible smoke expectation.
Keep smoke event, fixture event, payload name, tenant id, record id, write route, expected status, validation result, rollback result, and blocked payment probe together.
Show pass, hold, or block before backend route tests are written.
Keep buyer, supplier, and founder smoke paths role-aware.
Separate allowed audit-record writes from blocked payment custody probes.
Require rollback smoke visibility beside every allowed write smoke.
Use static smoke expectations until real auth, database, and API tests exist.

acceptance: Marketplace shows Backend Write Smoke Console after Storage Write Fixture Pack.
Buyer, supplier, and founder views each show smoke event, fixture event, payload name, tenant id, expected status, validation result, rollback result, and blocked payment probe.
Copy output explains smoke event, fixture event, payload name, tenant id, record id, write route, expected status, validation result, rollback result, and blocked payment route.
Build Phase shows the v179 Backend Write Smoke Console contract after the Storage Write Fixture Pack contract.
Docs include smoke states, smoke routes, blocked smoke routes, and required smoke fields.
Static check fails if the smoke UI, contract, JSON model, cache-bust token, or render functions are missing.
No backend route test starts without a visible smoke expectation or explicit hold.
